subtitle: Verified Gemini 3.7, recovered prompts, typography weights, all measured
description:
# Name That LLM Open Pool v11: 190,588 clean passages, ready to train

**v11 makes the labels more trustworthy and adds tools for choosing data.** `gemini-3.7-flash` now keeps only rows from a
documented Vertex AI route, because other APIs have served 3.8 under that name since 2026-10-08. Passages now carry a recovered prompt
id wherever one could be established (99% of rows), and a new `match_weight` column samples passages whose typography matches the real ones. Every passage in the main file passed all quality,
genre and licence checks, so you can train on the whole file with no filtering.

> **Please support this dataset with an upvote** if it helps you. Building and testing it took a lot of GPU time and
> effort, and votes help every competitor find the same free, clean data. If you think something here is wrong,
> please say so in the comments.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Passages | **190,588**, all 18 competition labels |
| Left out of the main file | 88,508 rows (see below; ids in `removed_rows.csv`) |
| Words per passage | median 99, range 36-275 |
| Source datasets | 55, all CC BY 4.0, CC BY-SA 4.0 or CC0 with verifiable provenance |
| Recovered prompts | 13,021 with prompt text; 592 answered by all 18 labels |
| Contains competition data? | **No.** No train copies, nothing close to train content, no answers to train prompts. |
| License | **CC BY-SA 4.0** |

## Why clean: the evidence

**1. The raw pool did not look like real passages.** Style rates in the competition's train.csv against the raw pool
(v7) and v9, with each label weighted equally:

| Feature | Real train | Raw pool v7 | v9 clean |
|---|---|---|---|
| ends with . ! ? or quote | 99.9% | 93.4% | 99.4% |
| uses we / our / us | 30.7% | 15.5% | 15.5% |
| uses I / me / my | 6.4% | 15.4% | 5.8% |
| contains a digit | 9.9% | 29.2% | 20.8% |
| contains ( ) | 1.1% | 11.4% | 4.1% |
| contains / | 0.3% | 11.6% | 1.6% |
| contains straight " | 4.0% | 19.1% | 8.7% |
| contains a colon | 52.1% | 54.0% | 46.6% |
| API dump or refusal | 0.0% | 8.2% | 0.0% |

The "we / our / us" gap does not move with cleaning. It comes from the host's prompts, not from junk.

**2. At equal size, clean data trains a better model.** A Qwen3-1.7B LoRA classifier was trained only on pool data,
with exactly 2,500 passages per label (45,000 in total) in every run. It was then scored on all 2,699 competition
train passages, whose prompts it never saw. Mean of 2 seeds:

| Training data (45k passages) | Balanced acc. | vs raw v1-5 |
|---|---|---|
| raw pool v1-5 | 0.466 | +0.000 |
| raw pool v1-7 | 0.464 | -0.001 |
| v1-5 minus hard junk | 0.474 | +0.009 |
| v1-5 minus junk and off-genre sources | 0.493 | +0.027 |
| v1-7 minus junk and off-genre sources | 0.492 | +0.026 |

**3. The dirtiest labels gain the most.** Across the 18 labels, the share of junk and off-genre text in a label's raw
sample correlates with its recall gain after cleaning (Spearman 0.64). kimi-k3 gained +16 recall points and
claude-opus-4-8 +13.

**4. Stricter filters were tested too** (same setup):

| Training data (45k passages) | Balanced acc. | vs clean v1-7, same seed | Seeds |
|---|---|---|---|
| v1-7 minus junk and off-genre sources | 0.492 | +0.000 | 2 |
| the same plus licence/provenance filters and 8.6k new passages | 0.492 | +0.000 | 2 |
| the previous row minus Kaggle Benchmarks proxy rows | 0.491 | -0.001 | 2 |
| the previous-but-one row minus the 30% least train-like passages per label | 0.488 | -0.004 | 2 |

v9 and v10 use the licence and provenance filters (no loss) and keep the Kaggle Benchmarks proxy rows, flagged in
`flag_kb_proxy`. Selecting only the most train-like passages did not help, so they do not filter on `style_score`.
All runs are in `dataq_results.csv`.

**5. Full-size check on the leaderboard.** The same DeBERTa-v3-large recipe was trained twice, changing only the pool:
raw v7 (254k passages) scored **0.585** public LB, clean v9 (193k passages) scored **0.587**. A quarter fewer passages,
same or slightly better score. Internal pool-based validation said v9 was worse, so do not judge data changes by it.

**6. New in v11: four more tests** (same setup, 2 seeds per training set, compared at the same seed with v10 minus the source that is no longer public). Each cell is the change in balanced
accuracy, with a 95% interval from resampling prompts. The interval does not include training randomness, so the two single-seed results are shown too.

| Change tested alone | All 150 train prompts | Half of prompts not used to fit it | Seed 0 / seed 1 | 2 answers per prompt | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| gemini-3.7 from Vertex AI sources only | +0.009 (+0.000 to +0.019) | +0.020 (+0.007 to +0.033) | +0.007 / +0.006 | +0.009 (-0.016 to +0.034) | **Adopted**: the main file now keeps only documented Vertex AI rows for this label |
| Sampling matched to real typography and length | +0.026 (+0.012 to +0.039) | +0.027 (+0.006 to +0.047) | +0.013 / +0.022 | +0.012 (-0.021 to +0.045) | **Added** as the optional `match_weight` column |
| Prompts with the most labels first | +0.009 (-0.005 to +0.022) | +0.024 (+0.002 to +0.044) | +0.016 / -0.003 | -0.006 (-0.036 to +0.027) | Not proven. `panel_labels` lets you try it |
| Adding prvsiyan extended rows | -0.009 (-0.023 to +0.004) | +0.013 (-0.005 to +0.032) | -0.001 / -0.005 | -0.004 (-0.035 to +0.026) | Not added (see correction below) |

- **Why the Gemini change:** within one large source, 3.7 and 3.8 rows could not be told apart (AUC 0.498), while 3.6 and 3.8 could (0.776).
  With Vertex-only rows, recall on real passages moved: 3.7 from 0.21 to 0.42, 3.8 from 0.59 to 0.64,
  and 3.6 fell from 0.63 to 0.47. The net effect is positive but this is not a free win for every label.
- **Why the typography weights:** on average a marker's rate sits 5.9 points from the real rate, and about 0 after weighting (by construction: the weights are fitted to these markers). Word hyphens on the
  Gemini labels: real 12%, pool 44%, weighted 12%. The test fitted its targets on one half of the train prompts and scored the other half.
  The column in this file uses all train prompts, so a validation on train.csv after using it will read slightly high.
- **Metric note:** the earlier prompt-centred score is not used for these decisions. With 17-18 answers per prompt it over-predicts some labels
  (baseline: 466 predictions of gemini-3.1 at 0.32 precision, none of kimi-k3). The "2 answers per prompt" column draws two passages per prompt and centres within the pair.
  Its intervals include zero: on that cut the Gemini and typography changes point the right way, but the test is not large enough to prove them alone.
- **Not tested as a whole:** each change was measured alone, and the 10,294 new passages were not part of these tests. All runs are in `dataq4_runs.csv` and `dataq4_paired.csv`.

## What is left out of the main file

| Reason (first matching) | Rows |
|---|---|
| Off-genre sources (chat logs, benchmark answers, reasoning traces) | 30,992 |
| Raw API responses stored as text (HTTP headers, JSON) | 13,114 |
| gemini-3.7-flash without a documented Vertex AI route: moved to `gemini37_unverified.parquet`, not deleted | 10,593 |
| Source dataset no longer public | 9,815 |
| prvsiyan extended rows: on-genre and well documented, tested in v11 with no gain (correction below) | 7,492 |
| Refusals | 6,939 |
| Licence or provenance risk (licence-excluded source re-uploaded as CC0, unverifiable origin) | 4,289 |
| Chat preambles, CJK text, length outside 36-275 words, same text with two labels | 2,197 |
| Cut off mid-sentence | 1,515 |
| Typography the label never uses in train (e.g. em dash for some Gemini labels) | 1,278 |
| Answers to the competition's train prompts | 284 |

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `ntl_open_pool.parquet` | the 190,588 clean passages |
| `gemini37_unverified.parquet` | 10,593 `gemini-3.7-flash` rows without a documented Vertex AI route, kept here so nothing is lost |
| `prompts.parquet` | text of the 13,021 recovered prompts, with how many labels answered each |
| `panel_gaps.csv` | 4,472 prompts with 10-17 labels and which labels are missing: **generate these to help the most** |
| `typography_match.csv` | per label and marker: real rate, pool rate, rate after `match_weight` |
| `dataq4_runs.csv`, `dataq4_paired.csv` | the v11 test runs and paired comparisons |
| `v11_append_log.csv` | how many candidate rows of the v11 sources each filter removed |
| `removed_rows.csv` | id and reason for every row removed from the raw pool |
| `removal_summary.csv` | rows removed per reason |
| `per_model.csv` | passages and sources per label |
| `sources.csv` | passages credited to each source dataset, with its licence |
| `dataq_results.csv` | every data-quality training run behind the numbers above |
| `style_gap.csv` | style rates: real train against raw and clean pool |
| `fig*.png` | the figures from the announcement post |

## Columns of `ntl_open_pool.parquet`

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | stable row id, unchanged since v1 |
| `text` | the passage |
| `model` | label as published by the source (one of the 18 competition labels) |
| `lab` | provider: anthropic, google, openai, zai, moonshot, qwen |
| `prompt_group` | source and the source's own prompt id. Unreliable across sources: use `prompt_canon` |
| `source_dataset` | Kaggle dataset credited for this passage |
| `source_file` | file inside that dataset |
| `source_license` | licence of `source_dataset` |
| `origin_hint` | the source's own src/source column, if it had one |
| `n_words` | whitespace word count |
| `also_in` | every source dataset containing this exact passage, separated by semicolons |
| `n_sources` | number of datasets in `also_in` |
| `max_cos_train` | highest TF-IDF cosine to any competition train passage (all below 0.3) |
| `max_sim_train_prompt` | highest TF-IDF cosine to any competition train prompt centroid |
| `style_score` | probability that a style-only model (punctuation, pronouns, rhythm, function words; no topic words) takes the passage for a real train passage |
| `flag_kb_proxy` | generated through the Kaggle Benchmarks proxy (69,745 rows). Allowed as public community data; drop with `df[~df.flag_kb_proxy]` to be strict |
| `flag_gemini37_routing_risk` | always False in the main file since v11; the 3.7 rows at risk are in `gemini37_unverified.parquet` |
| `flag_near_train_prompt`, `flag_train_prompt_regen` | always False since v9 (those rows were removed); kept so code written for older versions still runs |
| `prompt_canon` | recovered prompt id, shared across sources when it starts with `p`. Starts with `s` when known only inside one source; empty when unknown. Use it for group splits |
| `panel_labels` | number of labels that answered this prompt in this file (1-18) |
| `prompt_evidence` | how the prompt was found: `own_text` 31,516, `own_bank` 75,924, `other_text` 27,474, `centroid` 14,108 (matched by content; about 2% false matches in a hold-out test), `id_only` 39,641, `none` 1,925 |
| `match_weight` | sampling weight within a label, mean 1, so that typography and length match real passages. Use for sampling, not as a loss weight unless you test it |

## Quickstart

```python
import pandas as pd
pool = pd.read_parquet("/kaggle/input/name-that-llm-open-pool/ntl_open_pool.parquet")
print(len(pool), pool.model.value_counts())   # train on all of it

# or a fixed number per label, matched to real typography
sample = pool.groupby("model", group_keys=False).apply(
    lambda d: d.sample(min(2500, len(d)), weights="match_weight", random_state=0))
```

## Caveats

- **Labels are the publishers' claims.** Nothing here re-verifies which model produced a passage. The Gemini 3.7 route comes from each source's own documentation.
- **`gemini-3.7-flash` is now the smallest label** (3,278 passages from 4 sources), so its source mix is narrower.
- **Heavy typography weighting shrinks the usable sample:** the effective share of a label's rows under `match_weight` ranges from 30% to 79%.
- **The tests use a 1.7B model at a fixed 45k passages.** Larger models are more robust to noise, so the gain at full
  scale may be smaller. A full-size result will be posted in the discussion thread.
- **Not the hosts' prompts.** Cross-validation that mixes pool data into training reads a few points higher than the LB.
- **Uneven classes** (about 3k for `gemini-3.7-flash` up to about
  22k for `gemini-3.8-flash`). Use class weights or sampling.

## Corrections

- **prvsiyan's extended dataset is not off-genre.** v9 wrongly placed it in the off-genre row. It is on-genre and has some of the best provenance in this
  competition, including a served-model check on every call. Tested alone, adding its rows gave no gain, so they stay out, except its 266 Vertex AI
  `gemini-3.7-flash` rows, which are back in the main file (old ids kept where they had one). That no-gain result is about one small test, not about the author's work.
- **`flag_kb_proxy` was set per source, which marked 5,501 non-proxy rows as proxy.** Fixed from each source's own route column: alperen5252525 Vertex AI Gemini 2,573, arxitekton OpenRouter 2,846, earthmaker OpenRouter 82. Sources without a route column keep the flag they had, so treat it as an upper bound.
